h1: How Mindfulness Transformed My Parenting (And How It Can Help You Too)

p: I still remember the days when parenting felt like a never-ending to-do list—school runs, meals, tantrums, sibling squabbles, and the constant pressure to get everything "right." With two boys keeping me on my toes, I often found myself reacting instead of responding, feeling overwhelmed rather than present. But discovering mindfulness changed everything.

p: Mindfulness didn’t magically stop my children from bickering or erase the chaos of family life, but it did transform how I experienced it. Instead of feeling drained and frustrated, I learned how to meet the challenges with more patience, presence, and calm.
h3: The Power of a Pause

p: One of the biggest shifts was learning to pause. I used to jump straight into problem-solving mode—whether it was a forgotten PE kit or those damn book days where we needed a costume or a full on meltdown before bedtime, I often felt depleted and had no patience. Now, I take a breath ( not just one but a few long deep slow breaths). That pause gives me a moment to choose my response instead of reacting impulsively - its not easy and takes time and practice but its a great way to also models emotional regulation for my children, showing them that big feelings don’t have to control us and we are all human.
h3: Mindful Activities That Helped Me Stay Grounded

p: If you're a busy mum juggling a million things, I know the idea of adding mindfulness to your day might feel overwhelming. But it doesn’t have to be time-consuming or complicated. I like to think of them as mindful moments that become a simple easy effective part of your routine.  Here are a few simple practices that helped me, Mindfully Priya , become a calmer, more present parent:

p: Before, I would gulp down my tea while tidying up or scrolling my phone. Now, I make it a mindfulness moment.   I feel the warmth of the mug, take in the aroma, and savour the first sip. It’s a small act, but it reminds me to slow down and be present—even if just for two minutes. It during this ritual, I started to drink coffee for the first time in my 40's.  Before I was a tea lover, now, its black coffee all the way.
p: When the house feels chaotic, I do a quick five-senses check-in:

li: What can I taste? This grounds me in the present moment and helps me respond to my children with more clarity and patience. Although best done in the garden, than around screaming boys to start with.
h4: 3. Mindful Breathing With the Kids

p: When my boys are overwhelmed, instead of saying, "Calm down," we do various mindful breaths together, such as "balloon breath, finger breathing, lion breath" . It turns a tense moment into a connection point.

p: Lastly before bed, we share three things we’re grateful for that day. We keep them simple and think about acts of kindness we might have notice as well as appreciation of the simplest of things. It helps us end even the hardest days to focus on the good and also brings connection and a happier more calm way to fall asleep.
h2: The Real Gift of Mindfulness in Parenting

p: Mindfulness hasn’t made me a "perfect" mum (if such a thing exists), but it has made me a more present one. I still have stressful days, but I recover faster. I still get frustrated, but I can recognise it and shift my energy before it spills over.
p: And, most importantly, I’m showing my boys that emotions are okay, that self-care matters, and that being present is the greatest gift we can give to ourselves and each other.

p: If you’re a mum feeling overwhelmed, I promise you—just a few mindful moments a day can make a world of difference. Start small, be kind to yourself, and remember: the calm you seek isn’t found in controlling everything but in how you choose to meet the moment.

p: Want to bring more mindfulness into your parenting journey? Let’s connect . I support mums who want to parent with more calm, confidence, and presence. Reach out for a chat—I’d love to support you.

h1: The Journey of Priya Coaching Services

p: Starting a journey of self-discovery and healing is never easy, especially when life feels overwhelming. I know this well because I’ve walked that path myself. When burnout creeps in and transitions shake the very foundation of your daily life, it’s easy to lose sight of who you truly are. That’s why I created MindfullyPriya Coaching Services – to offer a gentle, supportive space where capable women, especially mothers, can find their way back to themselves and embrace a life filled with purpose and joy.
h2: How Priya Coaching Services Began

p: The idea for MidfullyPriya was born from my own experiences with burnout and the challenges of navigating life’s many transitions. I remember feeling exhausted, stretched thin, and disconnected from my own needs. It was during this time that I realised how important it is to have someone who truly understands and can guide you with empathy and practical tools.

p: I wanted to create a coaching service that wasn’t just about quick fixes or surface-level advice. Instead, it needed to be a journey – one that honours your unique story and helps you reconnect with your inner strength. That’s how MindfullyPriya came to life, with a focus on mindful, compassionate support tailored to women who are ready to reclaim their energy and joy.
span: A welcoming space for coaching sessions
h2: What Makes MindfullyPriya Coaching Different?

p: You might wonder, what sets my Coaching Services apart from other coaching options? The answer lies in the heart of the approach. It’s not just about setting goals or ticking boxes. It’s about you – your feelings, your struggles, and your dreams.
p: Here’s what you can expect when you choose Priya Coaching Services:
li: Personalised support : Every coaching plan is tailored to your specific needs and life situation.
li: Mindful techniques : We use mindfulness practices to help you stay present and reduce stress.
li: Practical tools : From time management to self-care routines, you’ll gain actionable strategies.
li: Empathy and encouragement : You’ll always feel heard, understood, and gently pushed towards growth.
li: Flexible sessions : Coaching fits around your busy life, not the other way around.
p: This approach has helped many women rediscover their confidence and find balance amid the chaos of motherhood and life changes.
h2: The Heart of Mindfully Priya Coaching

p: One of the most rewarding parts of this journey has been seeing how women transform through the coaching process. When I first started, I wanted to create a space where women could feel safe to explore their feelings without judgment. That’s why I’m proud to be part of Mindfully Priya – a community that values kindness, patience, and real connection.

p: Through this platform, I’ve been able to reach more women who are struggling with burnout, looking for a better balance in life, or facing big life transitions. It’s a reminder that none of us have to go through these challenges alone. Together, we can find clarity, strength, and a renewed sense of purpose.
span: Tools for mindful reflection and personal growth
h2: Practical Steps to Begin Your Own Journey
p: If you’re feeling overwhelmed or stuck, you might be wondering where to start. Here are some simple, practical steps that can help you begin your own journey towards healing and balance:
li: Pause and breathe : Take a moment each day to simply breathe deeply and check in with yourself.
li: Identify your needs : What parts of your life feel draining? What brings you joy? Write these down.
li: Set small goals : Choose one or two manageable changes to focus on, like a 5-minute morning meditation or a short walk.
li: Seek support : Whether it’s a coach, a friend, or a support group, don’t hesitate to reach out.
li: Celebrate progress : Acknowledge every small step forward – they add up to big changes.
p: Remember, this is your journey. It’s okay to move at your own pace and ask for help when you need it.
h2: Expanding Horizons: Corporate Wellbeing Programs

p: While my heart lies in supporting individual women, I also see the bigger picture. Burnout and stress don’t just affect personal lives – they impact workplaces too. That’s why MindfullyPrya is expanding to offer corporate wellbeing programs designed to help organisations support all their employees through life’s challenges or just allow them a little pause, calm and awareness to reset their nervous system.
p: These programs/workshops can focus on:
li: Building resilience and emotional intelligence
p: By bringing these tools into the workplace, we can create healthier, more supportive environments where women thrive both professionally and personally.

p: If you’ve read this far, I want you to know something important: you are not alone, and your feelings are valid. The journey to overcoming burnout and navigating life transitions is deeply personal, but it’s also one filled with hope and possibility.

p: Through MindfullyPriya, I’ve witnessed countless people reconnect with their true selves – the parts that are joyful, creative, and strong. It’s a beautiful transformation that starts with a single step: choosing to care for yourself.

p: If you’re ready to take that step, I invite you to explore how mindfully priya coaching can support you. Together, we can create a path that honours your unique story and leads you to a life of purpose and joy.
p: Remember, you deserve this journey. And I’m here to walk it with you.

h1: When Life Feels Loud: Mindfulness for Busy Mums Who Need a Moment to Breathe

p: Discover simple mindfulness practices for busy mums who want to find calm, balance, and presence in everyday chaos. Learn how small mindful pauses can help you reconnect with yourself, your children, and your sense of peace.
p: It’s 7:03 a.m. The kettle’s boiled - again. The lunchboxes aren’t packed. You’re replying to a work email while shouting reminders up the stairs.
p: By the time you finally sit down with your tea, it’s gone cold.

p: You love your family deeply, but some days it feels like you’re running on autopilot, juggling everyone’s needs while quietly losing sight of your own. You’re doing it all, yet feeling more disconnected than ever.
p: And beneath the busyness, there’s a whisper: “I just want a moment to breathe.”
p: That’s where mindfulness begins. Not as something new to add to your list but as something that helps you live differently with what’s already here.
p: Modern mums carry invisible to-do lists longer than the day itself.  You’re not just a parent; you’re the planner, the comforter, the teacher, the emotional anchor.
p: You hold everything yet rarely stop to ask: “How am I, really?”
p: Mindfulness gives you that pause.It helps you respond instead of react. It lets you notice the small, quiet moments that bring you back to yourself.
p: Because calm doesn’t come from getting it all done, it comes from noticing the moments in between.
p: Mindfulness isn’t about perfection, silence, or sitting cross-legged for hours.  It’s about presence meeting the moment as it is, without judgement.

p: It’s feeling your breath when you’re waiting in traffic.  It’s noticing your child’s laughter instead of rushing to clean up the mess.  It’s remembering that you’re allowed to pause before reacting.
p: Every mindful moment says: “I’m here. I’m enough. I’m doing my best.”
p: A simple mindful practice to anchor your day, no matter how busy it feels.
li: Pause. Stop wherever you are.
li: Inhale deeply through your nose, letting your shoulders rise.
li: Exhale slowly through your mouth, releasing tension, letting out a slight sigh
p: You can do this while waiting for the kettle, in the school queue, or before answering that next question or email.
p: Each breath reminds your body that it’s safe to slow down.
p: Take a quiet moment (even two minutes) to reflect:
li: Where do you feel most stretched thin right now - your mind, body, or heart?
li: What would calm really look like for you?
li: When was the last time you said “no” to something that drained you or “yes” to something that restored you?
li: What would change if you treated yourself with the same patience you give your child?
p: You don’t need perfect answers, only awareness. That’s where change begins.
p: So next time your child calls, “Mummy!” , pause before replying.  Take one deep breath.  Feel your feet on the ground.
p: Notice how even a single breath softens your response and brings presence back to the moment.
p: Mindfulness doesn’t require time — it simply asks for attention.
p: When you start slowing down, your children feel it too.  They sense your steadiness, your breath, your quiet confidence.
p: Your calm becomes the rhythm your family leans into.  And it start not with perfection but with one mindful breath.

h1: How Mindfulness Can Transform Your Life: Discover the Mindful Living Benefits

p: Life can feel overwhelming sometimes, especially when you're juggling so many roles and responsibilities. I know how it feels to be caught in the whirlwind of burnout and constant change. But what if I told you that a simple practice could help you find calm, clarity, and joy again? That’s where mindfulness comes in. It’s not just a buzzword; it’s a powerful tool that can truly transform your life.

p: Let me share with you how embracing mindfulness can bring about meaningful change, especially for capable women like you who are navigating life’s transitions. Together, we’ll explore the mindful living benefits and practical ways to weave mindfulness into your daily routine.
h2: What Is Mindfulness and Why Does It Matter?

p: Mindfulness is all about being present - fully aware of where you are and what you’re doing, without distraction or judgment. It’s about tuning into the moment, whether that’s noticing your breath, the sounds around you, or the sensations in your body.

p: Why does this matter? Because so often, we live on autopilot. We rush through our days, worrying about the past or the future, and miss out on the richness of the here and now. Mindfulness helps us break that cycle. It invites us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with ourselves.
p: For example, instead of feeling overwhelmed by a long to-do list, mindfulness encourages you to focus on one task at a time. This simple shift can reduce stress and increase your sense of control.
h2: The Mindful Living Benefits You Can Experience
p: When I first started practicing mindfulness, I noticed changes almost immediately. Here are some of the mindful living benefits that you might find helpful:
li: Reduced Stress and Anxiety : Mindfulness calms the nervous system. By focusing on the present, you stop spiralling into worries about what might happen.
li: Improved Emotional Resilience : You become better at handling difficult emotions without being overwhelmed.
li: Enhanced Focus and Clarity : Mindfulness trains your brain to concentrate, making it easier to complete tasks and make decisions.
li: Better Sleep : Mindfulness can quiet the mind before bed, helping you fall asleep faster and enjoy deeper rest.
li: Greater Self-Compassion : You learn to treat yourself with kindness, which is essential when you’re facing burnout or life changes.
p: These benefits aren’t just theoretical. They’re backed by research and real-life experiences. And the best part? You don’t need hours of practice each day to start feeling the difference.
span: Eye-level view of a peaceful garden with a single chair under a tree
h2: How to Start Practising Mindfulness Today
p: Starting mindfulness doesn’t have to be complicated. Here are some simple steps you can take right now:
li: Begin with Your Breath Take a few moments to notice your breathing. Feel the air entering and leaving your body. If your mind wanders, gently bring it back to your breath.
li: Use Mindful Pauses Throughout your day, pause for a few seconds to check in with yourself. Notice how you’re feeling physically and emotionally.
li: Engage Your Senses When eating, walking, or even washing dishes, pay attention to the sights, sounds, smells, and textures around you.
li: Create a Mindfulness Routine Set aside 5-10 minutes daily for a mindfulness practice. This could be guided meditation, gentle yoga, or simply sitting quietly.
li: Be Patient and Kind to Yourself Mindfulness is a skill that grows with practice. It’s normal for your mind to wander. Each time you bring it back, you’re strengthening your mindfulness muscle.

p: If you want to explore more tailored guidance, I highly recommend checking out resources from mindfully priya . Her approach is warm, practical, and especially supportive for women navigating burnout and life transitions.
h2: Mindfulness in Everyday Life: Practical Tips for Busy Women

p: I understand how hard it can be to find time for yourself when you’re managing so much. That’s why mindfulness needs to fit naturally into your life, not add more pressure. Here are some ways to make mindfulness part of your daily routine:
p: Start your day with a few deep breaths or a mindful sip of tea or coffee, using all your senses. This sets a calm tone for the hours ahead.
p: Whether it’s stretching, walking to work, or dancing, move your body with awareness. Notice how it feels and what it needs.
p: When talking with family or friends, give them your full attention. This deepens connections and reduces misunderstandings.
p: Take breaks from screens and social media. Use those moments to breathe or observe your surroundings.
p: Each evening, reflect on three things you’re grateful for. This simple habit shifts your focus to the positive.
p: Remember, mindfulness isn’t about perfection. It’s about presence. Even a few mindful moments can make a big difference.

h1: Stress Management for Mums: Practical Tips

p: Being a mum is one of the most rewarding experiences, but it can also be incredibly stressful. Between juggling family, work, and personal needs, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. I’ve been there myself, and I want to share some practical tips that have helped me find calm in the chaos. If you’re looking for gentle ways to ease your mind and regain balance, you’re in the right place.
h2: Understanding Stress Management for Mums

p: Stress doesn’t just come from big events; it often sneaks in through daily demands. When you’re constantly on the go, it’s easy to forget to pause and breathe. Recognising the signs of stress is the first step. You might notice feeling irritable, tired, or even physically tense. These are your body’s signals asking for a break.

p: One thing I’ve learned is that stress management for mums isn’t about doing everything perfectly or doing it all. It’s about finding small moments to care for yourself. This might mean setting boundaries, asking for help, or simply taking a few minutes to breathe deeply. Remember, you’re not alone in this journey.
span: A peaceful moment with a cup of tea
h2: Creating a Daily Routine That Supports You

p: A routine can be a mum’s best friend. It doesn’t have to be rigid or overwhelming. Instead, think of it as a gentle guide that helps you organise your day without adding pressure. Start by identifying the times when you feel most stressed and plan small breaks around those moments.

p: For example, I like to go for a short walk, even just for 15 minutes, which helps clear my mind, allows me to stretch, be with my thoughts, and be mindful of my environment.  It sets a calm tone for the day ahead. You might find that getting up 15 minutes before everyone else to enjoy a cuppa, journaling, or listening to your favourite music works just as well.
p: Here are a few ideas to build into your routine:
li: Morning mindfulness: Even 5 minutes of deep breathing can make a difference.
li: Scheduled breaks: Set alarms to remind yourself to pause and reset.
li: Evening wind-down: Create a relaxing bedtime ritual to improve sleep quality.
p: These small habits add up and help reduce the feeling of being overwhelmed.
h2: Practical Tips for Managing Stress as a Mum
p: When life feels like a whirlwind, practical strategies can be lifesavers. I want to share some simple yet effective tips that have helped me stay grounded.
li: Prioritise tasks: Not everything needs to be done today. Make a list and focus on what truly matters.
li: Ask for help: Whether it’s your partner, family, or friends, don’t hesitate to reach out. Sharing responsibilities lightens the load.
li: Limit screen time: Constant notifications can increase anxiety. Try to set boundaries around phone and social media use.
li: Move your body: Exercise releases feel-good hormones. Even a short walk or gentle yoga can boost your mood.
li: Practice gratitude: Taking a moment to appreciate small joys can shift your mindset from stress to positivity.
p: If you want to explore more about managing stress as a mum , there are wonderful resources and support networks available online.
span: Journaling as a tool for stress relief
h2: Nourishing Your Mind and Body

p: Stress can take a toll on both your mind and body, so it’s important to nourish both. Eating balanced meals, staying hydrated, and getting enough sleep are foundational. But beyond that, consider what feeds your soul.

p: For me, that’s spending time in nature, reading uplifting books, or connecting with friends who understand my journey. What brings you peace? Maybe it’s a hobby you’ve set aside or a creative outlet waiting to be rediscovered.

p: Try to carve out time each week for activities that recharge you. It might feel indulgent at first, but self-care is essential, not selfish. When you take care of yourself, you’re better equipped to care for others.
h2: Embracing Imperfection and Celebrating Progress

p: One of the hardest lessons I’ve learned is to let go of perfection. Life with children is unpredictable, and that’s okay. Instead of striving for flawless days, I focus on progress and moments of joy.
p: Celebrate the small wins, like getting through a tough morning or sharing a laugh with your child. These moments build resilience and remind you that you’re doing a great job.

p: If you ever feel overwhelmed, pause and remind yourself that stress is a natural response. It doesn’t define you or your worth. With gentle patience and practical steps, you can navigate this season with grace.

h1: From Overwhelmed Mum to Mindfully Me: Finding Balance in the Chaos

p: There was a time when “balance” meant making sure I had a minute to myself in the toilet before a toddler disaster struck. Work-life balance? Self-care? Those felt like things other people did and got right — mums, who weren’t drowning in housework, deadlines, and snack negotiations with two small but determined humans.

p: When I became a mum, I lost myself without even realising it. My identity slowly shifted from Priya to Mum , and while I adored my boys, I often felt like I was running on empty, feeling out of control and lost.  The pressure to be everything to everyone—nurturing mother, supportive wife, reliable friend, high-achieving professional — was relentless. Somewhere between keeping on top of school emails and responding to messages, I forgot to check in with the one person holding it all together: Me.

p: As a South Asian woman, motherhood came with an extra layer of complexity. I was raised with strong values around family, duty, and sacrifice—where a “good mother” is selfless, endlessly giving, and always putting her children first. And yet, I also grew up in the UK, where modern parenting celebrates independence, self-care, and balance.

p: The result? A constant tug-of-war between what I was taught, what society expects, and what I actually needed. Was I selfish for wanting time for myself? Was I a bad mum for wanting more? Was I failing if I didn’t follow the parenting advice passed down through generations?
p: It was exhausting. And confusing.
p: Motherhood is beautiful, but let’s be honest—it’s also relentless. The mental load is never-ending, the expectations are sky-high, and the guilt? It’s practically built-in.
li: Didn’t cook a fresh meal every night? Guilt.
li: Took time for yourself instead of spending every moment with the kids? Guilt.

p: For years, I thought that if I just tried harder , got more organised, woke up earlier than the kids (and I hate mornings) to seize the day that I’d finally feel in control. Instead, I just felt more exhausted. Something had to change.
h3: How Mindfulness & Coaching Changed Everything

p: My turning point came when I discovered mindfulness—not just as a practice, but as a way of being . And I don’t mean the “sit in silence and clear your mind” kind, I mean the real-life, practical, keep-you-sane-in-the-chaos, simple mindful moments kind.
p: Over the years mindfulness and coaching taught me that I didn’t have to live up to everyone else’s expectations. I just had to trust myself. I started to:
li: Tune out the noise of cultural and societal pressures.
li: Trust my instincts instead of waiting for validation.
li: Stop parenting from a place of fear (of judgment, of “getting it wrong”) and start parenting with confidence.
p: It wasn’t about adding more to my plate, it was about giving myself permission to do things my way.
p: As I deepened my mindfulness practice and coaching journey, something shifted.
li: I became a calmer, more present parent.
li: The endless guilt? It started to fade or I turned it around because guilt isn't a bad feeling as a mum, it just means I care.
li: The stress of trying to meet impossible expectations? I let it go.

li: And the biggest surprise? I started to find myself again—not just as a mum, but as Priya . The woman who still had dreams, passions, and a purpose beyond the daily grind. That shift changed everything.
p: Mothers today are expected to do it all —to be fully present, raise resilient kids, have a thriving career, keep the home running, and somehow stay sane. The pressure is unreal.

p: But here’s the truth: Balance isn’t about doing it all. It’s about knowing what truly matters and letting go of the rest. It’s about dropping the unrealistic expectations, setting boundaries that protect your energy, and realising that self-care isn’t selfish—it’s essential.
p: And when you take care of yourself, you’re not just a better mum, you’re a happier, more fulfilled YOU . And that changes everything. How you feel, how you show up and how you parent.

p: So if you’re reading this and feeling like you’ve lost yourself in the chaos of motherhood, know this: You don’t have to stay stuck. You don’t have to do it alone. And balance is possible — even if your tea still goes cold sometimes.

h1: Calm Techniques for Mums: Ways for Mums to Find Calm and Balance

p: Being a mum is one of the most rewarding experiences, but it can also be overwhelming. Between juggling family, work, and personal needs, it’s easy to feel stretched thin. I’ve been there too, feeling like the chaos might never end. But over time, I’ve discovered gentle ways to bring calm and balance back into my life. If you’re searching for practical, soothing strategies, you’re in the right place. Let’s explore some calm techniques for mums that can help you breathe easier and feel more centred.
h2: Simple Calm Techniques for Mums to Try Today

p: Finding calm doesn’t have to mean big changes or hours of meditation. Sometimes, small shifts in your daily routine can make a huge difference. Here are some easy calm techniques for mums that I’ve found truly helpful:

li: Mindful breathing: Take a moment to focus on your breath. Inhale slowly for four counts, hold for four, then exhale for four. Repeat a few times. This simple exercise can ground you when things feel hectic.

li: Create a quiet corner: Dedicate a small space in your home just for you. It could be a comfy chair by a window or a cosy nook with your favourite book. Having a personal retreat helps you recharge.
li: Set gentle boundaries: Saying no can be tough, but it’s essential. Protect your time and energy by kindly declining extra commitments that don’t serve your well-being.
li: Connect with nature: Even a short walk outside can refresh your mind. Notice the colours, sounds, and smells around you. Nature has a calming effect that’s hard to beat.
p: These techniques are simple but powerful. They remind me that calm is always within reach, even on the busiest days.
span: A peaceful corner for relaxation and calm
h2: What is the 7 7 7 Rule in Parenting?

p: You might have heard about the 7 7 7 rule in parenting, and it’s worth understanding because it’s a fantastic tool for managing stress and emotions. The rule is straightforward: when your child is upset or acting out, you take 7 deep breaths, count to 7, and then respond after 7 seconds. This pause helps you stay calm and thoughtful rather than reacting impulsively.

p: Why does this work? Because it gives your nervous system a chance to settle. When we’re stressed, our bodies go into fight or flight mode, making it harder to think clearly. The 7 7 7 rule interrupts that cycle and creates space for empathy and patience.

p: I’ve used this rule countless times, and it’s helped me respond with kindness instead of frustration. It’s a small practice that can transform your parenting moments and bring more peace to your home.
h2: How to Find Your Calm as a Mum in Everyday Life

p: Sometimes, the hardest part is knowing where to start. If you’re wondering how to find your calm as a mum, it’s about tuning into what your body and mind need. For me, it was about recognising the signs of burnout early and making self-care a priority.
p: Here are some ways to gently invite calm into your daily life:
li: Start your day with intention: Before the rush begins, take five minutes to set a positive intention. It could be as simple as “I will be patient today” or “I will take moments to breathe.”
li: Limit screen time: Constant notifications can increase stress. Try to have tech-free times, especially during meals or before bed.
li: Practice gratitude: Each evening, jot down three things you’re grateful for. This shifts your focus from overwhelm to appreciation.
li: Reach out for support: Don’t hesitate to ask for help from friends, family, or professionals. Sharing your feelings lightens the load.
p: If you want to explore more ways to find your calm as a mum, you can check out this helpful resource .
span: Journaling and tea as calming daily rituals
h2: Creating Balance: Practical Tips for Busy Mums

p: Balance might feel like a myth when you’re pulled in so many directions. But it’s possible to create a rhythm that honours both your needs and your family’s. Here are some practical tips that have helped me find that sweet spot:
li: Plan with flexibility: Use a planner or app to organise your week, but leave room for spontaneity. Life with kids is unpredictable, and that’s okay.
li: Prioritise sleep: It’s tempting to sacrifice rest, but sleep is the foundation of calm. Try to establish a bedtime routine that helps you unwind.
li: Incorporate movement: Whether it’s yoga, dancing, or a brisk walk, moving your body releases tension and boosts mood.
li: Make time for hobbies: Even 10 minutes a day spent on something you love can recharge your spirit.
li: Practice saying no: Protect your energy by declining non-essential tasks or events.
p: Remember, balance isn’t about perfection. It’s about making choices that feel right for you and your family.
h2: Embracing Self-Compassion on Your Journey

p: One of the most important calm techniques for mums is learning to be kind to yourself. Motherhood is full of challenges, and it’s easy to fall into the trap of self-criticism. But what if you treated yourself with the same warmth and understanding you offer your children?
p: Here’s how to nurture self-compassion:
li: Acknowledge your feelings: It’s okay to feel tired, frustrated, or overwhelmed. Naming your emotions helps you process them.
li: Speak gently to yourself: Replace harsh thoughts with encouraging words. For example, instead of “I’m failing,” try “I’m doing my best.”
li: Celebrate small wins: Every day brings moments of success, no matter how small. Recognise and appreciate them.
li: Allow yourself rest: Taking breaks isn’t selfish; it’s necessary for your wellbeing.
p: By embracing self-compassion, you create a foundation of calm that supports you through life’s ups and downs.

p: Finding calm and balance as a mum is a journey, not a destination. It’s about discovering what works for you and gently weaving those practices into your life. Remember, you’re not alone, and every step you take towards calm is a gift to yourself and your family. Take a deep breath, be kind to yourself, and know that peace is always within reach.
